natural_story_dialogue.evidence: Lesson 1 is an actual first meeting; Lesson 2 naturally justifies asking the name again after a brief first encounter; Lesson 3 explicitly frames the dialogue as practice instead of pretending the speakers are strangers.

surface_variation_transfer.evidence: Name and greeting functions recur as Hallo/Guten Morgen, Ich heiße/Ich bin and different farewell forms; later activities move to elevator, class and meeting contexts without showing a German answer cue.

learner_facing_pronunciation.evidence: The h target follows listen-notice-produce wording and tells the Persian-speaking learner not to drop the initial h rather than exposing phonetic jargon.

persian_speaker_contrast.evidence: The pronunciation note explicitly targets a predictable Persian-speaker issue: retaining audible word-initial h in Hallo.

novel_context_mastery.evidence: Lesson 4 activities require independent greeting, name question, polite response and farewell in a new meeting context, ending with one multi-function response without German scaffolding.

story_continuity.evidence: Lena and Raha meet only once as strangers; the following lessons acknowledge that they already know each other and use a justified repeat-name question or explicit rehearsal.

token_coverage.evidence: All 32 turn rows now carry non-empty token arrays; no turn uses an empty JSON_ARRAY token placeholder.

learner_speech_targets.evidence: Every learner turn contains a speech_target plus at least two accepted speech_alternatives so the Falou-style spoken response path is defined for the whole chapter.

distractor_quality.evidence: Each of the six word rows has three distinct meaning-related distractors and none repeats the correct Persian translation.

lesson_metadata.evidence: All four lessons now contain German title and description plus Persian title_translation and description_translation, with explicit exposure, explicit_form, retrieval and mastery roles.
